Dear day crew,
The training lead reviewed an idea about route planning earlier today, and I wanted to pass it on. The main point is simple: keep the handoff notes clear, keep the pet welfare checks visible, and make sure passengers get steady guidance before departure. When a traveler is uneasy, the supervisor should listen first and then confirm the next step without adding noise.

For routine desk work, the safest path is to slow down just enough to catch any mismatch in carrier details, feed notes, or cabin limits. If a case needs extra review, bring it forward early so the team can compare the booking record with what was said at check-in. That approach keeps the service calm and shared across the full journey, which is how Aurelia Skyways should operate at the Companion Animal Travel Desk.

Please keep using plain language in handovers and avoid assumptions when the pet file is incomplete. Clear notes help everyone protect the traveler, the animal, and the schedule without friction.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
